official_title.value: A Phase 3 Clinical Trial to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Twice-daily Applications of Delgocitinib Cream 20 mg/g Compared With Cream Vehicle for a 16-week Treatment Period in Adolescents 12-17 Years of Age With Moderate to Severe Chronic Hand Eczema (DELTA TEEN)

mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1) -- v1 extracted text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Delgocitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, inhibits the activity of JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2). JAK signaling involves recruitment of signal transducers and activators of transcription (STATs) to cytokine receptors, and activation and subsequent localization of STATs to the nucleus, leading to the expression of cytokine-responsive genes to induce specific biological responses in target cells. The exact mechanism of action of delgocitinib in the treatment of moderate to severe CHE is currently not known.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 9.4 Background treatment. No background treatment is required in this trial. The subjects should not change their usual skin care routine for the hands regarding use of emollients. However, emollients should preferably not be used on the affected areas within 2 hours before and after application of IMP.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Hierarchical evaluation, which is applied for the Bayesian analyses, will be used to control the overall type I error at a nominal one sided 2.5% level. This is built on the principle that the IGA-CHE TS superiority at Week 16 will have to be established before sequential testing for additional benefits (key secondary endpoints) related to efficacy. If superiority is claimed for the primary endpoint, then evaluation of the next endpoints will be done in a fixed sequential order as specified in Panel 4. This process will be repeated until no further tests are significant.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: The trial consists of a screening period, a treatment period, and a follow-up period. Screening period: minimum duration of 1 week and a maximum duration of 4 weeks... Eligible subjects will be randomised 3:1 to treatment with delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g or cream vehicle... the subjects will be required to return to the trial site for the visits scheduled at Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, and 16... Follow-up period: Subjects will be followed-up via phone ... approximately 2 weeks after the last IMP application. Duration of trial participation will be approximately 22 weeks, consisting of a screening period of up to 4 weeks, a treatment period of 16 weeks, and a safety follow-up period of 2 weeks.

value.rationale: Rescue treatment is permitted if medically necessary to control intolerable CHE symptoms, at investigator discretion. Otherwise-prohibited medications/procedures are allowed as rescue but require IMP discontinuation.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 9.5 Rescue treatment. If medically necessary (i.e. to control intolerable CHE symptoms), rescue treatment for CHE may be prescribed to trial subjects at the discretion of the investigator. ... If rescue treatment is initiated, the subject must stop treatment with IMP immediately and will not be allowed to restart treatment with IMP. Subjects who discontinue IMP will be asked to attend an early termination visit, a follow-up visit ... and also the primary endpoint visit at Week 16.
